razonamiento:
I need to design a letter with impossible geometry, like a Penrose-triangle-style "A" whose strokes connect in ways that can't actually exist in 3D space, pure SVG with no surrounding text.

Computing coordinates for an equilateral outer triangle and its inset inner triangle to form the Penrose bars, planning to break the ring at one corner so the shading creates the illusion of impossibility.

I'll use overlapping rectangular bars with a cyclic over-under pattern instead of mitred corners—bar1 over bar2, bar2 over bar3, bar3 over bar1—achieved by drawing them in sequence then re-drawing a clipped piece at the corner where the order needs to flip.

I'm reconsidering the geometry as thick lines along a centerline triangle, extending each bar slightly past its vertex so the square ends overlap cleanly, giving a triangular shape with protruding corner ends.

Working through the overlap ordering, I find that painter order L, R, Bt actually gives R>L at top, Bt>R at BR, Bt>L at BL — not a proper cycle, so I need L clipped at BL to make it cyclic: top R>L, BR Bt>R, BL L>Bt. I'll also add shading with varied stroke colors and a lighter inner stripe for a rounded look.

Now I'm skipping the letter-terminal idea and just computing the extended endpoints for the L-shape strokes, extending each segment by a fixed offset beyond its corner to overlap cleanly with the adjacent shapes.

Extending both L and Bt endpoints to overlap cleanly, then re-clipping L near the BL corner so it paints over Bt without bleeding into R. I'm picking a muted palette—dark charcoal, mid gray, light gray—against a warm off-white background, and considering adding a dark outline stroke beneath each bar for definition.
